name: Combined Immunodeficiency Due to Partial RAG1 Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Partial RAG1 Deficiency

criteria.description: Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in the RAG1 gene with residual recombinase activity
Reduced but detectable T and B lymphocyte counts with impaired V(D)J recombination
Recurrent severe infections, autoimmune manifestations, or granulomatous disease in infancy or early childhood
Exclusion of other causes of combined immunodeficiency by clinical and laboratory evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of biallelic pathogenic RAG1 variants with compatible immunophenotype and clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Functional assays demonstrating partial recombinase activity support diagnosis

searchTerms: combined T and B cell immune failure
low B cell count in blood
decreased white blood cells that make antibodies
immune system destroying red blood cells
red blood cell breakdown from antibodies

common.symptomName: Neutropenia in presence of anti-neutropil antibodies

laboratory: Reduced T and B lymphocyte counts with abnormal T cell receptor excision circles (TRECs)
Hypogammaglobulinemia with low immunoglobulin levels (IgG, IgA, IgM)
Autoimmune cytopenias evidenced by Coombs positive hemolytic anemia or thrombocytopenia
imaging: Chest radiograph may show bronchiectasis or interstitial lung disease
CT scan may reveal granulomatous lesions in lungs or lymphoid tissues
other: Flow cytometry demonstrating abnormal lymphocyte subsets
Bone marrow biopsy may show lymphoid hypoplasia

distinguishingFeatures: Complete absence of T and B cells
Early onset with life-threatening infections in first months of life
Absent or severely reduced recombinase activity
Later onset, typically in adolescence or adulthood
Normal or near-normal T cell counts

redFlags: Recurrent severe infections with opportunistic pathogens
references: Schuetz C, Huck K, Gudowius S, et al. An immunodeficiency disease with RAG mutations and granulomas. N Engl J Med. 2008;358(19):2030-2038.
